CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to review symptom logs and response to treatment since the last appointment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns today for his follow-up visit, bringing with him a detailed log of his symptoms and medication responses over the past month. He reports that his anxiety has remained stable since his last appointment, with no significant exacerbations. He continues to engage in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), which he finds beneficial for coping with work-related stress, particularly during high-pressure situations. However, he still experiences situational anxiety, especially when presenting to senior management.
Regarding his insomnia, Mr. Smith reports that trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime remains effective for initiating sleep, but nocturnal awakenings persist, averaging three times per night. He has maintained his melatonin dosage at 10 mg, which he believes has slightly improved his overall sleep quality. Nonetheless, he wakes feeling tired and is concerned about the cumulative effects of sleep disruption on his daily functioning.
His tension-type headaches have shown slight improvement, now occurring twice weekly. He rates the intensity as moderate, with episodes averaging 5 out of 10 on the pain scale. He continues to use ibuprofen 600 mg as needed, which provides adequate relief. Mr. Smith expresses interest in preventive strategies and is open to discussing alternative treatment options.
Mr. Smith continues to report fatigue, which he attributes to both work stress and sleep disturbances. He feels that bupropion at 150 mg daily has helped stabilize his energy levels somewhat, but he still experiences fluctuations, particularly in the afternoons.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 6. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (continued) 7. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 8. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 9. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to maintain a healthy lifestyle, with regular physical activity including yoga and walking. He has successfully reduced his caffeine intake and is committed to mindfulness practices, although work stress occasionally interferes with his routine.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety remains stable; sleep quality is still a concern; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency decreased; intensity rated as moderate; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, with some variations; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears slightly fatigued but engaged; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain CBT sessions; assess progress at the next visit. Lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety will remain on the regimen. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Monitor melatonin effects; consider increasing dosage if sleep quality does not improve in the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. Discuss potential referral to a neurologist for evaluation of preventive therapies if headache frequency or intensity does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage regular exercise and stress management techniques. Re-evaluate fatigue levels and consider additional interventions if there is no improvement by the next appointment.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-06-01 to continue monitoring symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to keep a detailed log of his symptoms, medication responses, and any potential triggers for his anxiety or headaches to facilitate ongoing management.
